A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MergeGuard work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after the references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes Supplementary Material A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, image-generation and language-model experiments, including defense comparisons, stage ablations and adaptive attacks.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports mask-evaluation timings and supplementary image-generation and code-output examples.

M1.justification: The L2-regularized finetuning, critical-layer masking and masked task-vector subtraction remain unchanged. The expanded loss presentation and supplementary Transformer description explain existing components without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 and Figure 5 add an SD1.5 generation scenario pairing an Animate defender with a Simpsons free-rider, beyond the retained Naruto/WikiArt scenario. The eight classification datasets and three language benchmarks are unchanged.

E2.justification: PaRaMS remains the sole quantitative defense baseline. The evaluated WA, TA, TIES, AdaMerging and DARE+TIES comparisons are retained; the additional generation scenario uses the existing model-state controls.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a separate evaluation of Stage 2 mask-computation time in minutes. Existing benchmark metrics and stated hyperparameters remain unchanged; Appendix A's dataset counts newly document settings rather than establish changed splits.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds computational-cost analysis across datasets and models, while Appendix D supplies additional generation cases and a concrete redundant-code example. The stage ablation in Table 4 and adaptive-attack evaluation in Table 5 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new timing tables report point estimates and averages across settings without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the results displayed in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. New results include mask-evaluation times of 51.60–557.28 minutes for vision datasets and 293.08–641.20 minutes for LLM settings, plus the qualitative outputs in Figures 5–6.

T1.justification: The task-vector assumptions, curvature-misalignment argument and loss-interference relation are retained. The vision loss is moved into a numbered equation, and Appendix B explains standard MLP and attention computations; neither supplies a new theoretical result or correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dual-stage defense contribution, claimed accuracy degradation of up to 90%, limited standalone utility loss and resistance to two adaptive attacks. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets mask-evaluation cost as increasing with dataset size and argues that this overhead is acceptable for protection against free-riders. The main mechanism explanations and discussion of discriminative versus generative behavior remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses CPU/GPU hardware, Ubuntu and Python versions, and dataset class counts, train/test counts and resolutions. Appendix C supplies preprocessing-cost information. These improve documentation of retained experiments without establishing changes to their implementation.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 49 works and retain the same positioning relative to model-merging research and PaRaMS. The appendix reuses existing dataset references rather than introducing new related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands the loss explanation, changes an author affiliation and adds organized supplementary sections A–D. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds supplementary Tables 6–8 and Figures 5–6, relocates the unchanged workflow Figure 2 from page 5 to page 4, and adjusts equation display and spacing. Existing main figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies appendix material referenced but absent in the supplied v1, making the computing environment, dataset composition and substantial mask-evaluation overhead inspectable. Additional image and code examples improve evidential completeness. These are useful transparency gains, while the main effectiveness results, theoretical support and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
